summary: Earthtone is a Webapp that turns NASA EIC visualizations into live music. A 3D globe steps through 93 frames (29 Oct to 13 Nov 2026) of 5 daily EIC layers: temperature, wind, precipitation and clouds, humidity, and PM2.5. Click anywhere on the globe and the music takes exactly one step a frame, so what you see and what you hear are the same moment. To make the frames playable, we decode their colors back into numbers by matching each pixel against the published colorbars (checked against NASA POWER climatology at 20 points, decoded temperature is within 1.06 degree celsius and wind within 0.83m/s). Every place has its own key and mode. Temperature sets the melody, wind the tempo, rain the plucked notes, clouds the reverb, humidity the warmth of the chords, and PM2.5 a grainy texture. Unusual warmth or cold adds audible tension. Earthtone makes climate data something you can hear and compare, place by place.
details:
What it does? Earthtone is a webapp that turns NASA EIC visualizations into live music. Plays five daily layers: temperature, wind, precipitation and clouds, humidity, and PM2.5. Clicking on any place starts the music and the music advances a step every frame, so what you see and what you hear are synchronized.

How it works? A build-time pipeline downloads the frames from NASA SVS and decodes their colors back into values by matching each pixel against published colorbars. It's checked against NASA POWER and the accuracy of temperature is within 1.06 degrees celsius and 0.83m/s for wind. NASA POWER climatology supplies the “normal” for comparison. A bundled copy is used if POWER is unreachable.

Benefits!? Earthtone makes Earth data something you can hear and compare, not only LOOK at. This also suits museum exhibits and classrooms very well.

Tools: Next.js, TypeScript, three.js, Tone.js, and sharp. Deployed on Vercel.

Any Creativity? YES! Instead of using the visualizations as decoration, Earthtone reads them as data and plays them as if frame-locked to the visuals.

Values are labeled "approximate" and may not be completely accurate but everything has been checked for highest accuracy possible. Caching, Ratelimits within the application help prevent flooding NASA APIs from our application.
